title: God Is a God of Restoration
speaker: Ryan Baird
summary: Sin breaks things, but it is not too late. Turning to the Lord brings restoration, beginning with a right relationship with God.
exhortation: For some reason, as I was reading this, the Lord brought to mind my uncle David. My uncle David is a wonderful, godly man. He's the kind of Christian you can't walk away from without feeling the brightness of his faith rub off on you a little.

I distinctly remember being at his house one time and going for a short walk with him to a park near his house with my son Kai. I was sharing some very real, serious struggles I was having. He told me stories from a ministry he had to a prison. He would often go to a particular prison and minister to the men there, and one of the things he would often tell them is that God is a God of restoration. God restores. Turning to follow the Lord brings restoration, and it brings good into your life.

Now, this doesn't mean that everything gets fixed. He was saying this with compassion toward me, because the reality is that sin breaks things. There's darkness in this world, and sin has wrecked a lot. But much of your life can be restored. Your life can be fruitful again if you will turn to the Lord. That has always stuck with me.

As I read this passage, I know there have been many times in my life when I've been tempted to think, "It's too late. I can't have these things. I can't have a wife who is like a fruitful vine in my house. I can't eat the fruit of my labor anymore. I won't have children like olive shoots around my table." If you're not careful, that can lead to despair upon despair. And God does not want that for you. He wants you to turn and put your faith and your trust in him, and the Lord will restore you.

Not every circumstance in your life will change. But the most important thing can: you can be restored to a right relationship with your Creator by putting your faith and trust in Jesus Christ. So turn to the Lord this morning. Don't give in to despair. Don't stop fighting. Trust in the Lord, and he can restore what's been broken by sin, by the power of his grace.
prayer: Lord, we're so grateful that though our sin destroys and messes everything up, you came to heal. You came to set straight and make right the things that are crooked. And though we feel the consequences of our sin, it's not out of wrath or anger, but out of a desire for restoration.

God, you are moving us toward a time when all things will be made right: every tear wiped away, every sin gone, every wrong made right. Thank you that we can look to you and put our hope in this glorious future, in the forgiveness and the restoration we have in you. We pray that we would live today in gratefulness and in hope that you are working. In Jesus' name, amen.
